thread.title: Daily markets morning round-up: E-mini S&P, gold, crude & Treasuries

title: Daily markets morning round-up: E-mini S&P, gold, crude & Treasuries
text:
E-mini S&P 500 (June) 
Yesterday’s close (Thursday, April 19): Settled at 2693, down 16.75 
Fundamentals : Yesterday’s weakness was on the largest volume day of the week. The banks notched a great session and Amazon, Google and Facebook all posted solid gains. However, it was Apple (AAPL) and Consumer Goods along with Healthcare that dragged down the other half of the market. After price action traded back below the 50-day moving average and first key support, the selling was contained by major three-star support at 2679.75. The low was 2681.50 and as technical as the session had become, it was a Mueller headline that ripped the tape higher in the last half an hour; Deputy Attorney General Rosenstein told President Trump last week that he was not a target of Special Counsel Mueller’s investigation or raid of Trump’s lawyer Michael Cohen. 
Additionally, it was said that President Trump told those close to him that he does not plan to fire either Rosenstein or Mueller since he is not a target. This paves the way for a very interesting Friday session that has so far held within yesterday’s late range. While there is are no major releases on the economic calendar today there is a full board of earnings before the bell; GE, Honeywell, Schlumberger, Waste Management and others. Chicago Fed President Evans speaks at 8:40 a.m. Central and current San Francisco Fed President and soon to be New York Fed President Williams speaks at 10:15 a.m. Central. President Trump tweeted this morning that Republicans are trying to make the recent tax cuts permanent and this seems to have buoyed the market from overnight lows. 
Technicals : We remain Neutral and believe that this market can be traded from both sides. Yesterday was a prime example of such as there were multiple setups to sell while major three-star support proved to be the buying opportunity. Crude oil (June) 
Yesterday’s close: Not available 
Fundamentals : Price action reached a new swing high of $69.55 per barre l before retreating yesterday. OPEC met this morning and referencing the production cuts, Saudi Oil Minister Al Falih said that “The journey is far from over, and they still have a long time to go.” Russian Oil Minister Novak pointed to the positivity from the cuts, but also noted the risks if they stopped short of fully reaching their goals. The groundwork was laid for a friendly Friday session. However, President Trump put the kibosh on that quickly with a tweet that read, “Looks like OPEC is at it again. With record amounts of oil all over the place, including the fully loaded ships at sea, oil prices are artificially very high! No good and will not be accepted!” Responses from OPEC officials are just now trickling out. While there is geopolitical premium built into this market, we must not forget the relief that was also seen earlier the week. We maintain that the risk is to the upside as the market enters a seasonally bullish time of year. Baker Hughes rig data is due at noon Central. The dollar is higher today and continued strength does pose a headwind to the bull camp. 
Technicals : Crude oil is falling back this morning and does remain susceptible to strong waves of selling due to the over-extended net-long position. While we believe the path of least resistance remains higher, traders must manage risk knowing that these waves can come. 
Gold (June) 
Yesterday’s close: Settled at 1348.8, down 4.7 
Fundamentals : The U.S dollar has been creeping higher over the last 48 hours and this has weighed directly on gold. Still, the metal has done absolutely nothing wrong and remains fundamentally constructive in the face of reduced geopolitical worries and an equity market that has rallied about 6% from its low less than one month ago. There is no major economic data on the calendar to close out the week, but we look to Chicago Fed President Evans speaks at 8:40 a.m. Central and current San Francisco Fed President and soon to be New York Fed President Williams speaks at 10:15 a.m. Central. 
Technicals : Price action has flirted around and settled right at our pivot of $1,348.8 per oz. We point to this level upon today’s settlement and close above it clearly signals to us that the bull camp is in the immediate term driver’s seat. Traders must continue to watch silver, if today’s pull back from resistance. 
Natural gas (May) 
Yesterday’s close: Settled at 2.695, down 0.073 
Fundamentals : Yesterday’s storage read showed a bigger draw than expected to come in at -36 bcf versus a range of -23 bcf to -26 bcf. Still, prices had their worst down day in weeks; weather is seasonally stabilizing, and the focus is forward-looking to injection season.

10-year Treasuries (June) 
Yesterday’s close: Settled at 119’265, down 0’10 
Fundamentals : The retreat in Treasury prices continue as the longer end yields play catchup to the shorter end; the yield curve is steeping. There is no economic data on the docket today, but we look to Chicago Fed President Evans speaks at 8:40 a.m. Central and current San Francisco Fed President and soon to be New York Fed President Williams speaks at 10:15 a.m. Central. We maintain two ideas; the yield curve will flatten and there is extremely strong fundamental and technical support just below the market aligning with near 3%. 
Technicals : At these levels, value is creeping into the long side, however, bulls must stay patient for now. Price action is below first key support and can easily see further weakness.
